subject: Storing multiple parameters in one (or more) CEL files

messages.author: bc1f4b339b21de43
messages.subject: Storing multiple parameters in one (or more) CEL files
parts:
Hi list,

I am writing a fitting procedure which calculates a set of parameters
from a training sample and then applies it to new samples. I generate 6
parameters for each probe. I would like to store these in a convenient
way.

I have been looking at ParameterCel{File|Set} and their subclasses, but
I haven't found any that store more than 2 floats and 1 integer
(corresponding to intensities, stdvs and pixels in the CEL file),
whereas I have 6 floats.

Are there any examples of storing this sort of information? Does it
sound like I am heading in the right direction? Any other suggestions
appreciated.

Cheers,
Tim Keighley

On Tue, Mar 18, 2008 at 12:13 AM, <Tim.Ke...@csiro.au> wrote:
>
> Hi list,
>
> I am writing a fitting procedure which calculates a set of parameters
> from a training sample and then applies it to new samples. I generate 6
> parameters for each probe. I would like to store these in a convenient
> way.
>
> I have been looking at ParameterCel{File|Set} and their subclasses, but
> I haven't found any that store more than 2 floats and 1 integer
> (corresponding to intensities, stdvs and pixels in the CEL file),
> whereas I have 6 floats.
>
> Are there any examples of storing this sort of information? Does it
> sound like I am heading in the right direction? Any other suggestions
> appreciated.

Yes, we use (binary/XDA) CEL files to store parameter estimates. They
hold 2 floats and 1 short (in total 4+4+2=10 bytes). These can be
used to encode/decode anything. The main rationale we had when we
decided to store estimates in CEL files was that we could utilize the
same framework (affxparser et al, CDF, CEL, ...) for reading and
writing data. The probe affinities estimates are naturally stored as
a CEL file, since they (in most cases) map one-to-one to probes. The
chip effects are store in smaller CEL files mapped by the monocell CDF
(which is uniquely defined by the main CDF).

The only way to store more information that 10 bytes per probe is to
use more CEL files. However, I strongly discourage you from doing
that, mainly because I want to have the leeway for aroma.affymetrix
diverge from the above in a future (a far future) version.

Instead, the easiest way is to just use (R.utils') saveObject() and
loadObject() to store/read parameter estimates. They work similar to
save()/load() but don't "dump" the object to the global environment.
Try and you'll understand. I use saveObject()/loadObject() to store
estimates in GladModel/CbsModel; that way I could
postpone/procrastinate/avoid having to define a file format. The
catch is that you cannot subset on, say, units when reading/writing,
but they are fast and if you want still want to subset by units and
read a lot of arrays, use loadObject() for the first array, then
subset and discard the rest, the loadObject() for next array and so
on. That is probably good enough and I don't think the I/O will be
too bad.

There was an early decision to stay away from defining new file
formats, mainly because there are already plenty of them out there and
we're not helping out by introducing new ones. However, for
annotation data such as UGP=(unit, chromosome, position), UFP=(unit,
PCR fragment length) I finally made the decision that we can do better
with binary versions than slow ragged ASCII files. For this I have
been working on the AromaUnitTabularBinaryFile class - it maps data
indexed by units (as ordered in the CDF). See
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/aromatabularbinaryfile
for more information. Note that it is still in an alpha/beta version;
since no one else is using the file format I can modify it and just
provide updated versions of the UGP and UFL files to the users. When
more people using it, I loose the option and backward compatibility
becomes an issue. However, I think it is rather flexible right now,
which is why I invite you to have a look at it. There is no
AromaCellTabularBinaryFile, but there is the superclass
AromaTabularBinaryFile which is more generic. If you go down this
path, please share your experience with me/others.

Hope this helps

Henrik
